summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis and a history of hepatic encephalopathy was admitted after presenting with right facial droop, right-sided weakness, and slurred speech, initially concerning for stroke. Imaging including CT and MRI of the brain showed no acute infarction, hemorrhage, or mass. Neurological symptoms were variable and inconsistent with a focal lesion. She was diagnosed with a flare of hepatic encephalopathy, likely contributing to her neurologic presentation. Lactulose was increased to four times daily, resulting in improved mental clarity and stability of symptoms. Liver enzymes transiently elevated but trended downward, and abdominal ultrasound showed no ascites or vascular abnormalities. Blood culture showed a likely contaminant, not requiring treatment. She was discharged home with continued lactulose, instructions to avoid sedating medications, and follow-up for lab monitoring and transplant evaluation.
